_comment: PROVIDER PLUG-IN for the `shariah-governance` role — the in-house alternative, for institutions whose ISSC secretariat keeps the register itself (a board-secretariat system, a minute book, a governance share). It closes a specific hole: governance/identities.template.json gives every ISSC seat a `reconciliation_source` of docs/governance/issc-register.json, and that file sits inside the repository the coding agent can write. An agent that adds a sixth seat, or edits an hsa_approval_ref to match a signature, makes a committee out of a file. This provider makes the register an EXPORT the secretariat asserts, reconciled against the file the gate reads. It rules on nothing: Shari'ah is decided by the scholars whose names the register carries — the register only says who they are and under what approval they sit. To adopt: record the choice in docs/governance/provider-selection.json, copy this file to docs/governance/adapters/, point it at your secretariat's system, and wire the export that fills activation_evidence.
capability: The institution's own ISSC register — seats, HSA approval references, appointment instruments, and the resolutions an approval cites — exported by the secretariat that maintains it, for reconciliation against the register the gate reads

role_fit._comment: Stated plainly so the choice is made with open eyes. Neither line argues for or against — they are the trade being accepted.
role_fit.strength: ISSC minutes and appointment instruments never leave the institution, which is usually non-negotiable for a body that sits under confidentiality; the secretariat that files the resolution is the same desk that exports it, so there is no second copy of the committee's record to disagree with the first
role_fit.limitation: IT IS SELF-ASSERTED, and calling it a system of record does not change that. The export and the repository can share a maintainer, so the separation must be MANUFACTURED: the export must run under a secretariat identity the coding agent cannot assume, and write to a store the agent cannot edit. Absent that, docs/governance/issc-register.json is the agent's word for who sits on the committee — which is exactly the hole the role exists to close

reconciliation._comment: Reconcile on the composition AND its provenance. Matching seat_count alone passes a register where one scholar was quietly swapped for another; matching member_ids alone passes a seat whose approval reference was edited to fit a signature already collected.

activation_evidence._comment: ADOPT: fill from a real export + the tamper probe. The tamper probe is the decisive one — it proves the RECONCILIATION bites, not that an export ran. A register that reconciles against a file the same identity wrote proves nothing at all.
activation_evidence.fetched_at: ADOPT: timestamp of your register export
activation_evidence.exported_by: ADOPT: the secretariat identity that owns the register — must NOT be assumable by the coding agent
activation_evidence.tamper_probe: ADOPT: 'rejected' once you have tested that editing docs/governance/issc-register.json away from the exported register (add a seat, change an approval reference) fails the build
